goal: Implement and live-verify one hash-addressed Manifest v2 binding CatalogRevision, Exact Registry, Gear/Community Releases and runtime dependencies; cut every active equipment-simulation consumer to that binding; retire legacy runtime readers; and complete CAS, rollback, WeChat and three-party closure.
userValue: Every equipment browse, import, save and simulation action uses one coherent current-season equipment truth instead of silently mixing the active release with whichever catalog or exact cache happens to be latest.
nonGoals: Do not change the existing WeChat entry routes or merge equipment editing into the SimC page.
Do not infer any of the 55 Phase 2 partial references or promote them to ready.
Do not change the 26 supported versus 14 unsupported specialization policy.
Do not rewrite historical SimulationSnapshot, task or result rows.
Do not claim global data health is green while independent components remain partial.

mustChange: Add Manifest v2 identity, persistence, immutable Catalog/Exact binding and candidate preview.
Cut Catalog, Community, Resolver, Profile, Snapshot, task and owned health consumers to one binding.
Replace runtime latest/staging reads with exact Manifest-bound identities.
Add zero-caller legacy-reader inventory, bounded shadow, CAS promotion/rollback and real WeChat evidence.
mustNotChange: Do not alter user entry routes, template IDs, owner isolation or historical task results.
Do not mutate sealed v1 releases, Catalog, Exact, Snapshot or result rows.
Do not allow v1, staging or latest-cache fallback to appear as a v2 success.
Do not switch the generation-32 pointer before immutable candidate verification passes.
riskUnknown: The Catalog BrowseVariant to source-variant compatibility adapter may expose progression or option parity gaps.
Manifest v2 rollback must preserve v1 readability without permitting a mixed-version response.
Owned health migration may reveal independent partial states that remain outside this phase.
evidenceRequired: RED/GREEN Manifest v2, migration, append-only store, binding and consumer tests.
40-spec browse, 80-template import/loadout, 26/14 real SimC, deterministic snapshot/result reuse and no-fallback candidate evidence.
Zero legacy runtime caller inventory, resource limits, service/timer state, pointer fence and rollback/restore proof.
Official WeChat self-test, full Harness, PR CI, merge, deployment, local/origin/cloud parity and cleanup.

ownership.factOwner: Manifest v2 owns only the immutable dependency join; CatalogRevision owns browse membership; Exact Registry owns concrete template instances; existing Resolver owns legality; SimulationSnapshot owns execution bytes.

engineeringHealth.reason: This phase changes the production authority boundary and active PostgreSQL pointer. TDD, immutable candidate, full consumer shadow, real SimC, CAS rollback, official WeChat and three-party parity are mandatory.

acceptanceEvidence: Every successful equipment-simulation consumer reports and validates one Manifest v2 dependency vector.
All 40 specializations browse, all 80 Community templates classify, 26 supported profiles execute and 14 unsupported profiles block deterministically.
The 55 evidence-gap references remain explicit partial and cannot produce ready loadouts.
Legacy runtime latest/staging reader caller count is zero before deletion.
CAS promote, v1 rollback and v2 restore pass API, task and identity smokes.
Official WeChat self-test and local/origin/cloud/Manifest/runtime parity pass.

decisionLog.decision: The user authorized Codex to self-test and continue through later stages without waiting for manual confirmation.
Manifest v1 remains readable only for the generation-32 baseline and rollback; Manifest v2 is the first contract allowed to claim Catalog and Exact Registry binding.
The source Gear Release remains a bound provenance and enhancement/Resolver authority, while CatalogRevision becomes the public browse identity; the backend owns compatibility mapping.
A successful Phase 4 response may not use latest exact, mutable staging or an unbound compatibility reader.

Catalog v2 BrowseVariant identity includes a canonical exact shape of item level, bonus IDs and static facts in addition to item and progression. Equal observed aliases may collapse; different shapes within one progression remain distinct, and a Community import alias must be sealed into the selected shape.

A verified Community import carries a server-generated privacy-safe templateAuthorityIdentity that binds one Exact Registry template group. Missing or ambiguous identity blocks; projected UI gear fields and client-provided content hashes cannot be used to guess exact identity.
